To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crustal thickness is controlled by magma supply, and that the magma supply is controlled by mantle upwelling.

the crustal thickness of the propagating segment at 21.50°N is governed by lateral magma transfer, and the propagation rate seems to depend on the amount of magma reaching the propagating segment ends.

the crustal thickness of the segment controlled by the propagating ridge segment is controlled by the melt supply, and that the propagation rate is controlled by the amount that reaches the segment end.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crustal structure of the actively propagating TAMMAR segment at 21. 5°N on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and how the crustal structure is controlled by melt distribution and upwelling.
the evolution of the crustal structure during ridge propagation.
the evolution of a propagating ridge segment, the mechanisms controlling the onset of propagation, the propagation rate and the propagation length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crustal architecture along propagating ridge segments is controlled by the amount and distribution of mantle-derived melt.
ridge propagation occurs when the magma supply is focused at the segment ends.
ridge propagation is a consequence of the complex interaction of the melt supply, melt distribution, and the strength of mantle upwelling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
propagation initiation is due to an increase in melt supply, while propagation length is controlled by the upwelling strength and melt supply.
the crustal thickness is a key factor for the initiation and propagation of ridge segments, and thus for the segmentation of slow‐spreading ridge segments over time.
the crustal evolution is controlled by the magma supply and that the propagation is controlled by the melt supply and the strength of the upwelling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crustal structure is controlled by the melt supply, and that the crustal thickness is the main control for the propagation length.
the structure of the crust along a rapidly propagating segment is governed by melt supply and upwelling.
the crustal architecture of a ridge segment controlled by rapid propagation is fundamentally different from a segment not controlled by propagation.
